label: Mirrors
description: History pictured as a mirror that reflects the past (and even the future), associated with the image of naked truth.
source_domain: optics / reflection (mirror, glass)
historical_function: history as a faithful reflection of truth and of the past
example_patterns: history is the mirror of the past

label: Perspectives
description: History as a multifaceted object to be examined from many sides; knowledge tied to a vantage point (Gadamer's range of vision).
source_domain: vision / viewpoint (vantage point, angle)
historical_function: historical knowledge as bound to a situated perspective

label: Constructions
description: The historian's work as creation and construction, not discovery or recovery (Oakeshott).
source_domain: building / making (construction, architecture)
historical_function: history as something the historian constructs rather than merely finds

label: Masters and Teachers
description: History as master and teacher — mother of truth, witness and counsel — yet also the ironic lesson that nothing is learned from it.
source_domain: pedagogy (teaching, mastery; historia magistra vitae)
historical_function: history as teacher and store of exemplary lessons

label: Clio Transfigured
description: The classical muse Clio recast in modern guise — the umbrella for trains, motion, and tribunal imagery that secularizes and dynamizes history.
source_domain: mythology reconfigured (the muse Clio made modern)
historical_function: the personified muse of history transfigured into modern, dynamic forms

label: Railways and Trains
description: The train of time, railway of progress, and locomotive of history — and the revolution reimagined as the emergency brake.
source_domain: rail transport / locomotion (train, railway, locomotive)
historical_function: history/progress/revolution as a locomotive racing forward to make up lost time

label: History in Motion
description: History in motion — the centaur of philosophy of history, the world-soul on horseback, stallions, masses and revolutionaries in action.
source_domain: motion / animals and vehicles (horses, centaur, triumphal car)
historical_function: history personified as a force or figure in visible movement

label: Court of Justice and Dustbin
description: History as the world's court of justice that will judge or absolve actors — and conversely as the dustbin into which the past is thrown.
source_domain: law and waste (tribunal, court of justice; dustbin, rubbish)
historical_function: history as moral tribunal that judges and absolves, or as a dustbin discarding the past

label: Counter-Metaphors
description: Counter-metaphors that turn the tables — life that must judge history; the Angel of History seeing progress as a heap of rubble.
source_domain: critical inversion (Nietzsche's life over history; Benjamin's Angel)
historical_function: metaphors that contest the idealization and authority of History/progress

label: Turns, Levels, Professions, Territories, Borders
description: History mapped as a territory with porous borders to philosophy, rhetoric, theology, geography and politics — subject to 'turns' and lacking natural frontiers.
source_domain: territory and boundaries (borders, fields, professions, turns)
historical_function: history as a domain with shifting borders and turns among neighbouring disciplines

label: Memory of Time / Time of Memory
description: Time and memory caught in mutual implication — as in expressions where the thing (wind, river, time) seems separable from its very movement.
source_domain: substance vs. process (wind blows, river flows, time passes)
historical_function: the reflexive entanglement of time and memory

label: Clio, Chronos, and Kairos
description: Clio writing on the back of Chronos; time the devourer against memory the preserver; the fullness or ripeness of Kairos.
source_domain: mythology (Clio, Chronos the devourer, Kairos the opportune moment)
historical_function: tension between recording memory, devouring linear time, and the ripe moment

label: Circles, Lines, and Points
description: Time figured through shapes: classical cycles vs. Christian linearity, the point of eternity or the messianic instant, and the spiral.
source_domain: geometry (circle, line, point, spiral)
historical_function: the figural shape of time — cyclical, linear, punctual, or spiral

label: Water, Rivers, and Seas
description: One of the oldest images of time: the river that flows yet endures (Heraclitus), the sea of language and understanding, the historian as boatman on the stream of time.
source_domain: hydrology (river, stream, current, sea, ocean)
historical_function: time/history as flowing water — continuity within change

label: Atmospheres and Thresholds
description: A period figured as an enveloping atmosphere or spiritual climate — the spirit of the age, the air one breathes, the threshold between climates.
source_domain: meteorology / air (atmosphere, climate, Zeitgeist)
historical_function: an epoch as a pervasive atmosphere one breathes

label: Levels, Sediments, Strata
description: Historical time stratified into surface events and deep, slow structures — Unamuno's intrahistory, Braudel's longue durée, Koselleck's layers of time.
source_domain: geology (strata, sediment, seabed, layers)
historical_function: a layered, depth model of historical time

label: Turbulent Times
description: Time as turbulent flow and as shattered fragments — currents dragging us off, shards cutting the mind, palimpsests and folds.
source_domain: turbulence and shattering (whirl, shards, washing machine)
historical_function: chaotic, fragmented, accelerated temporality

label: A Deluge of Memory
description: The memory boom as a trickle swelling into a flood and a sea; sites of memory as shells left when the sea recedes; inscription as sowing.
source_domain: flood + inscription (trickle to flood; wax tablet, aviary)
historical_function: the late-20th-century memory boom figured as a rising deluge

label: The Essential Triad
description: The essential triad: each present contains a past, a present, and a future — the knot tying time's dimensions together.
source_domain: lived time (three 'todays'; knot/bundle)
historical_function: every historical present binds together three distinct times

label: Past and Present
description: Past and present in mutual definition — history as a 'science of the present' that connects what is otherwise unconnected.
source_domain: relational time (connection of presents)
historical_function: the past exists for the sake of, and through, the present

label: A Foreign Country
description: The past as a foreign country where they do things differently — naming both the deep cut from the present and the urge to stitch it closed.
source_domain: geography / travel (a foreign country abroad)
historical_function: the alterity of the past and the modern wish to suture the cut
example_patterns: the past is a foreign country

label: The Living and the Dead
description: History as a tomb that lays the dead past to rest in scriptural graves; or, against that, the past living on in spectral form.
source_domain: death and burial (tomb, corpse, ghost, decay)
historical_function: history as burial of the dead past — or as its ghostly survival

label: Distances and Dimensions
description: Distances and dimensions of time — the historian ascends from the present toward origins; retrospection is a double-edged sword risking the condescension of posterity.
source_domain: spatial distance / optics (ascent, descent, retrospect)
historical_function: the historian's retrospective vantage and its hazards

label: Present and Future
description: Present and future — the present as window, watchtower, blind spot or trap from which the empirically unverifiable future is glimpsed.
source_domain: verifiability and vision (open window, watchtower, eye of the hurricane)
historical_function: the present's vantage onto an unverifiable future

label: Lights
description: Lights — the past as a lamp at the entrance to the future; the guiding star of progress that may have ceased to shine (a dead star).
source_domain: light / illumination (lamp, star, beacon, darkness)
historical_function: the past or reason illuminating the future

label: Seeds
description: Seeds — agricultural and obstetric images: the present as seed, bud, or pregnancy of a coming future; revolution as birth and the midwife of a new society.
source_domain: botany / generation (seed, bud, flower, harvest, pregnancy)
historical_function: the present as the seed or bud of a future yet to germinate
example_patterns: the bud of a future flower

label: Horizons
description: Horizons — the future as an open, advancing horizon line; Koselleck's horizon of expectation (Erwartungshorizont) and Gadamer's fusion of horizons (Horizontverschmelzung); a later vertical sense links horizon to geological strata.
source_domain: geography / vision of the horizon (and, later, geological 'horizons'/strata)
historical_function: the future and the historicity of understanding figured as a moving, expanding horizon
uncertainty_note: The source `metaphors_javier.md` truncates mid-3.3.3 ('Every living thing can become healthy, strong, and fruitful only with…'). Description and cues recovered from the book body (Ch. 3, 'Present and future'): Nietzsche's '…only within a horizon', plus Koselleck and Gadamer.

label: Sources and Traces
description: Sources and traces — historians 'drink' from sources that may be pure or contaminated, abundant or drying up; memory as a heap of broken fragments.
source_domain: springs / fountains and traces (water source, fragments)
historical_function: historical evidence figured as sources one drinks from and as traces

label: Events and Facts
description: Events and facts — events as surface foam and crests carried by the tides of history, or as a 'black hole' of meaning; facts as established constructions.
source_domain: surface phenomena (foam, crests, black hole)
historical_function: the distinction between events that happen and facts that are established

label: Processes and Structures
description: Processes and structures — the event as a single note on the keyboard of structure; history as natural process: waves, glacial drift, tectonic movement, alluvial deposit.
source_domain: nature and music (keyboard, waves, glacial drift, tectonics)
historical_function: history as deep process and structure beneath the events

label: Revolution
description: Revolution figured as a careering carriage rushing from precipice to precipice, a brake against speeding culture, or supra-gigantic forces crushing or carrying individuals.
source_domain: vehicles and forces (carriage, locomotive, brake, supra-gigantic forces)
historical_function: revolution as runaway vehicle or overwhelming force dragging humanity

label: Crisis
description: Crisis as the great divide bridging one epoch and another, a nexus of growth reached by leaps, a moment of change that lights up all levels of social reality.
source_domain: medicine / turning point / bridge (crisis, growth-nexus, epoch-bridge)
historical_function: crisis as a decisive turning point that illuminates an epoch

label: Modernity
description: Modernity — the parent grouping for the family of metaphors by which the modern age pictures itself (revelation, hidden agency, rationalization, storm, contract, network, machine).
source_domain: umbrella for modern self-imagery (multiple source domains)
historical_function: grouping node for the self-images of the modern age

label: Revelation, Discovery, Disappointment
description: Revelation, discovery, disappointment — Copernican and cosmological discovery empties the universe of meaning, turning it into a silent galactic desert and decentring humanity.
source_domain: cosmology / discovery (Copernican decentering, galactic desert)
historical_function: modernity as disenchanting revelation and consequent disappointment

label: Action and Mastery
description: Action and mastery — history moved by concealed hands: Smith's invisible hand, Kant's ruse of nature, Hegel's cunning of reason.
source_domain: hidden agency (invisible hand, ruse of nature, cunning of reason)
historical_function: modern history as steered by an impersonal, cunning agency

label: Rationalization and Secularization
description: Rationalization and secularization — the Cartesian light of reason; Foucault's image of 'man' erased like a face drawn in sand at the sea's edge.
source_domain: light and erosion (light of reason; a face erased in sand)
historical_function: modernity as rationalization and secularization

label: A Perennial Gale
description: A perennial gale — modernity as ceaseless storm and maelstrom of systems, where the artist must distil the eternal from the transitory.
source_domain: wind and storm (gale, maelstrom, whirlwind)
historical_function: modernity as a perpetual, creative-destructive storm

label: The Pile of Sand and the Contract
description: The pile of sand and the contract — society without a common goal as a heap of sand scattered by the slightest puff, against which the contract binds.
source_domain: granular matter and contract (a pile of sand; the social contract)
historical_function: modern society as a fragile aggregate needing a binding contract

label: Globalization and Great Acceleration
description: Globalization and Great Acceleration — the global village and global city; society as web, net, and flows; liquid modernity and the nervous system of the planet.
source_domain: networks and flows (web, net, global village/city, liquid)
historical_function: globalization figured as networks, flows, and a shrinking connected world

label: Acceleration
description: Acceleration — the exponential curve and spiral, Rostow's economic 'take-off', and the paradox of a 'frenetic standstill' or 'frozen time'.
source_domain: kinetics / aeronautics / geometry (exponential curve, spiral, take-off)
historical_function: modernity as ever-increasing speed — the Great Acceleration
uncertainty_note: Corresponds to the unnumbered '#### Acceleration' block under 5.3.6 in the curated md; assigned id 5.3.6.1 to make it addressable. The book groups acceleration within 5.3.6 'Globalization and Great Acceleration'.

label: Perverse Effects and Counter-Metaphors
description: Perverse effects and counter-metaphors — modernity as a runaway engine, iron cage turned gas chamber, shipwreck, mega-machine, insatiable Moloch, time bomb, or terminal cancer.
source_domain: machines, disease, catastrophe (runaway engine, iron cage, shipwreck, cancer)
historical_function: critical counter-metaphors for modernity's perverse effects

label: Progress, Advancement, Development
description: Progress, advancement, development — history as walking or climbing forward; yet Marx's progress as the pagan idol drinking nectar from the skulls of the slain.
source_domain: walking forward / climbing (progredi; ivy climbing; the march of progress)
historical_function: progress as forward movement and ascent — with its critics

label: Decadence and Decline
description: Decadence and decline — downward-bending and falling imagery; with the death of meaning in history, the idea of progress dies too.
source_domain: falling and bending downward (declinare, cadere; sunset, decay)
historical_function: decline as falling and decay — even the death of progress itself

label: Tradition and Transition
description: Tradition and transition — tradition as what is handed down (outside which there is only plagiarism); transition as the mind's passage from the absolute to the category of becoming.
source_domain: handing down and crossing over (tradere, transire)
historical_function: tradition as transmission and transition as passage into the historical

label: Shards
description: The future and historical time as broken glass, fragments, and shards after the collapse of unified progress narratives.
source_domain: broken glass / fragments / debris / shattered temporal continuity
historical_function: figures fragmented, plural, disconnected, or catastrophic futures
uncertainty_note: Accepted from the book’s explicit numbered section 3.3.4.
